item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 18, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Finance Stack on why the bubble won't just pop — a bouncy castle kept up by five fans, hyperscalers now spending 115% of cash flow on buildout, $680B of AI debt, and the circular deals (Nvidia's $105B OpenAI-linked guarantee); Krugman panel on the numbers — $1T+ capex since 2024, $6T planned through 2030, ~$300B revenues vs $2-3T needed; Ed Zitron on the Jensen-manufactured bubble and circular financing; Eli on the Anthropic IPO, 7x oversubscribed while its valuation slid from $2T to ~$1.1-1.4T. Supply/demand: Dividend Data on Nvidia's customers and the capex ramp (Microsoft $150B, Amazon $200B); FinVid on signed contracts and prepayments, the agentic-AI inference inflection, and compute constrained through 2028. Watchlist: Schwab's Jay Woods on Kress's first call and the $150 level; Dividend Data on Nvidia's supply-chain moat and deep-value case ($209 at 25x P/E); Options Ryan on Costco at 53x for 10% growth vs Nvidia at 16x for 93%; TeslaGuy on AMD and Broadcom as the new semi leaders; Tom Lee on a November 18 bottom by the waterfall-decline math and buying the AI dip.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 17, 2026
item.description: NVDA earnings day: Stas on the $115.8B blowout ($2.68 EPS, $130B Q4 guide, $150B buyback) and why he's still not buying more; Bloomberg analysts on the margin-guide question and $2.4B of Hopper shipped to China; Schwab on the hyperscaler vs neocloud revenue split, the SEC probe into international sales, and Rubin; Dividend Data on NVDA at its cheapest forward P/E in 10 years; Tom Lee and Dan Ives on whether an AI crack takes down the market; Beth Kindig's $20T-by-2030 thesis, memory sold out to end of decade. Supply/demand: FinVid's compute-constrained-through-2028 case - no GPUs sitting dark, buildout into contracted demand.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 16, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Steven Van Metre - Blackstone's datacenter giant QTS went looking for $800M and came back with $300M, lenders walking away from the best credit in the business; The Young Turks - Elon Musk admits the AI datacenter buildout is a giant bubble, debt markets have shut off the neoclouds and 'guppy level death' is coming; Capital Insight - Ed Dowd says AI was 45% of the market, the tech bubble has already burst, and Nvidia will miss within six months as hyperscalers go negative free cash flow; Neal K. Shah - Nvidia's circular financing machine and over $530B in shadow liabilities; RedGamingTech - the Commerce Department's new remote-access chip rules, SemiAnalysis cutting AI accelerator capex 20-40% through 2030, and Goldman desk confidence fading. Supply/demand: Steven Van Metre - the credit cycle is turning, buyers are full, banks are stuck holding loans, and BofA says deals are being pushed to 2027; The Young Turks - even Jensen Huang admits there isn't enough capital for the neoclouds, CoreWeave down 41% with distressed bonds; Verified Investing - the week ahead: Warsh, Nvidia earnings, and the Anthropic IPO. Pricing: RedGamingTech - RTX 5090s around $6,500, still 3x MSRP, but used prices down 20-30% and availability improving. Watchlist: Finance Deep Dive - Dan Ives is still buying Nvidia, on Colette Kress and the CEO candidates; Verified Investing - Nvidia ahead of earnings; Joe Blogs - the sell-off spreading across Asia with TSMC down 5.7% and Nvidia down $1.9T from its October peak; Joe Blogs - Nvidia's earnings preview, $108-109B expected with zero China revenue assumed, and CoreWeave's $709M quarterly loss on $846M of interest; Meet Kevin - the SemiAnalysis bear case, a $1.6T spending cut, and why it's a delay, not a cancellation.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 15, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Meerkat Explains - the market can't decide if the bubble popped, CoreWeave is paying 16% to borrow with lenders pricing a coin-flip chance it repays, and the whole tower rests on a chipmaker's promise to rent the chips itself; Meerkat - a bubble is a price kept alive by darkness, the AI giants were funded by a sealed private room passing the parcel at ever-higher prices while the labs lose $1.60 per dollar of revenue; Meerkat - Burry has reportedly bet against the biggest names, the Mag 7 are worth $24T and a third of the average 401(k) sits in them, and the takeaway is the bubble hasn't failed to pop, it has failed to be looked at; The Bigger Board - a day-by-day scenario of the bubble bursting tomorrow, from the trigger to the stock market's first day. Supply/demand: Eli the Computer Guy - OpenAI pushed its IPO to 2027 and raised only $11B of a $30B round, Anthropic's record IPO is a week away with a collective shrug, and Amazon is warehousing $5B a month of Nvidia gear with nowhere to plug it in; Eli - SoftBank lost $3.7B cancelling 13 GW of gas turbine orders for AI data centers, more than six Hoover Dams of capacity; Eli - SoftBank is unwinding turbine contracts, Microsoft unwound its Oracle AI rental, and Accenture and Apple have slashed employee AI token spending from $1,000 a month to $29 and $300 a day to $25; Just Have a Think - the Sierra Club projects proposed AI data centers could push US grid emissions up 42% to 2.1 billion tonnes by 2030. Watchlist: FinVid/King Lip - Nvidia's brain-drain risk as AMD and Broadcom call its engineers, the AI capex cycle is a durable multi-year engine not a bubble, and Anthropic's IPO is over six times oversubscribed; FinVid - the bull case: the world is compute-constrained through 2028, no GPUs sit dark, agentic AI is inflecting inference demand, and physical AI is Nvidia's next multi-trillion leg; Mohsin Ali - Nvidia fell 32% in five and a half weeks, $1.7T of market value gone, and the full timeline from the spy reports to Huang's Nov 12 resignation; Mohsin Ali - what to watch Tuesday: Vera Rubin shipments, interim CEO Colette Kress facing questions on the investigation, the reported $105B OpenAI guarantee, and a split Street with HSBC at $170 and Raymond James at $515; Smart Money Bro - bigger than Jensen Huang: why he's still buying Nvidia stock.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 14, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Finance Stack - nearly one in five Korean adults own Samsung, the market has lost nearly half its value, and AI is now a fifth to a third of US growth with the Mag 7 a third of the S&P; Finance Stack - the other side: hyperscalers can afford their debts, the IMF's AI crash scenario is a 2000-size problem not 2008, but SoftBank and Thiel sold all their Nvidia and Burry is short; TheOneLanceB - the correction is hot but not irrationally exuberant, and the Anthropic IPO needs a mildly more cautious stance. Supply/demand: Eli the Computer Guy - Microsoft is winding down its Oracle AI cloud rental on older-generation Nvidia chips and rethinking billions in cloud partnerships, because AI architecture is still immature; Eli - Nvidia wants to sell the whole AI factory as the product, and Microsoft is pushing back Iron deliveries and tightening oversight of neoclouds; Market Signal - Cisco raised hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue to $9B with networking up 40%, Applied Materials posted record $10.4B revenue up 53% with wafer-fab equipment demand at a record pace, and Samsung won back-to-back 2nm AI ASIC orders. Watchlist: Market Signal - a sea of red, $560B wiped off the board, Nvidia down $600B in its worst week on record at about $162; The Creative Investor - the Jensen-comeback rumor, the year-end rally case with Nvidia earnings Tuesday and the Anthropic IPO Monday, and AI-lab valuations that will never justify themselves; Dividend Talks - Broadcom is number one as hyperscalers build their own chips, with a $516 DCF, and the full ranking wrap-up: TSM and Lam S-tier, Micron, SK Hynix and SanDisk opportunity names, Nvidia a measured accumulation.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 13, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Ed Zitron (The Tech Report) - Nvidia's unrivaled free cash flow funded the circular financing that propped up the AI ecosystem, and with Huang gone that world doesn't return; Tom Nash - Jevons paradox means cheaper compute drives more demand, and the CUDA moat didn't leave with Jensen's leather jacket. Watchlist: Parkev Tatevosian - what the next Nvidia CEO needs: TSMC/Micron/SK Hynix supply-chain ties and the customer relationships behind the circular financing; ChartEquity - why Nvidia is falling ahead of Nov 17 earnings, the $125 bear case vs the $250 bull case; Tom Lee - does Nvidia still belong in portfolios, the real risk is employees, and watch LinkedIn job postings; The Hostile Takeover - earnings graded: Nebius, Applied Materials, Cerebras; Motley Fool - Bloomberg: Nvidia working with an outside firm to identify CEO candidates, Tom Gardner on the board, the national-security angle and the stock's fall from $240 to $170.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 12, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: Ed Zitron - Nvidia was the bank of AI, and with Huang gone the circular financing that propped up the ecosystem is over (The Tech Report); Paul's Hardware - is the bubble bursting? Trust no one selling a certain answer, and if AI hits a wall, data-center demand falls off hard; TheTechnicalTraders - Nvidia down 11% today, 36% from the highs, and Anthropic's ~$90B IPO looks like a feeding frenzy. Supply/demand: Innovation Uncovered - hyperscalers spent ~$200B on capex in Q3, Meta's free cash flow went negative and buybacks hit the lowest since 2017, so the buildout is now debt-funded; Nick Saraev - OpenAI runs ~100% on Nvidia while Anthropic is only ~33% and is building custom silicon, shifting the compute balance; NBC DFW - Georgia's data centers will double state power demand in five years, and the fight is over who pays for the grid. Watchlist: CBS - the timeline of Huang's resignation, from the affair admissions to the board's move; Schwab/Jablonski - were investors buying Nvidia or Jensen Huang? Demand for compute is intact and a lot of AI stocks are on sale; Schwab/Hanks - the facts: $5.7T to $4.2T market cap, Ives' $225 target without Huang, AMD +23% and Broadcom +17% this week; Tom Lee on CNBC - watch talent retention, the thing that would tell you if Nvidia is weathering this.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Nov 11, 2026
item.description: AI bubble: The Tech Report panel asks 'is AI in a bubble?' - value accrues to chipmakers, frontier models face a pricing equilibrium, like the web in 2001; Ed Dowd - the tech bubble has already burst, semis are in a bear market, Nvidia to miss as hyperscalers turn free-cash-flow negative (CapitalCosm); Sabine Hossenfelder - the AI boom is financed on borrowed money, $466B in nine months, and the key test is getting users to subscribe. Supply/demand: CoreWeave's earnings sparked the rally - revenue beat, backlog jumped to $132.5B, cheaper contract-backed financing at 7-7.5% plus $9B in customer prepayments (The Hostile Takeover); WSJ - midterm voters pushed back on data centers, and Texas, Ohio and Georgia hold ~40% of US capacity; George Packer - the backlash could crash a stock market held up by AI, while wage earners see little benefit (Amanpour and Company). Watchlist: CBS - Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang; NBC4 - the scandal in brief: stock down 4% Monday, ~$190B wiped out, board investigation and shareholder lawsuit; Parkev Tatevosian - Dan Ives puts 25-30% downside on Nvidia if Huang goes, yet Nvidia trades at a forward P/E of 10.5, cheapest in years; Tyler Hill - the premarket rally recap and the levels that matter (AMD above 580, Micron above $829), CoreWeave's report saved the sector; The Hostile Takeover - rally breadth: SMH +5.7%, Micron +13%, Marvell +10%, Nvidia +3.9%, Applied Materials +7%, AMD +8.9%, Broadcom +5.3% - bottoms form on bad news.
